summary: 41-year-old man with known L4/5 disc: 2 days of bilateral sciatica, saddle numbness, urinary hesitancy and reduced anal tone; post-void residual 180 mL.

inputs.chiefComplaint: Back pain going down both legs and numbness in the bottom
inputs.hpi: Known L4/5 disc prolapse with left sciatica for 6 weeks. For 2 days pain down both legs, numbness around the back passage and genitals, difficulty starting to pass urine and reduced feeling when passing urine. Bowels not opened for 2 days.

exam.neuro: Reduced pinprick sensation in the perianal and perineal area (S3–S5), reduced ankle reflexes bilaterally, plantarflexion 4/5 bilaterally. Reduced anal tone on PR.
exam.abdomen: Bladder not palpable; post-void bladder scan residual 180 mL.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Cauda equina syndrome — incomplete (CES-I), L4/5 disc
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Suspected incomplete cauda equina syndrome (bilateral sciatica, saddle anaesthesia, urinary hesitancy, reduced anal tone): emergency MRI and immediate spinal surgical referral.

mustNotMiss.knownGapNote: Web: PANE has no spinal node; top 3 inguinal hernia, cholecystitis, GORD. Symptom inference ranks lumbar disc disease / sciatica, not CES.
mustNotMiss.proposedFix: Add medical-emergency diseases to lib/pane-engine (or a separate medical-mimic layer) driven by labs/vitals/chips, or show the symptom-inference leader beside the PANE top 3 when PANE has no matching node.

mustInclude.knownGapNote: Web: No bladder scan / post-void residual.
mustInclude.proposedFix: Add neurological safety prompts to clinical-inference.ts keyed on symptoms/HPI text (FAST → CT head + stroke team; thunderclap → CT head ± LP/CTA + neurosurgery; meningism/purpura → blood cultures + IV ceftriaxone now; saddle anaesthesia/retention → emergency MRI + spinal team; cancer + back pain/weakness → MRI whole spine + dexamethasone + MSCC coordinator).

guideline.name: SBNS/BASS — Standards of care for investigation and management of cauda equina syndrome
guideline.section: Suspected CES (bilateral radicular pain, saddle sensory change, bladder/bowel/sexual dysfunction): emergency MRI; immediate discussion with the on-call spinal surgical team; decompression as soon as possible; do not wait for urinary retention (retention indicates CES-R); post-void residual bladder scan as part of assessment
guideline.citation: Society of British Neurological Surgeons & British Association of Spine Surgeons. Standards of care for investigation and management of cauda equina syndrome. 2018. See also: GIRFT National Suspected Cauda Equina Syndrome Pathway, 2023.

rationale: SBNS/BASS 2018 and GIRFT 2023: emergency MRI and immediate spinal surgical discussion before retention develops.
